title: Alex Hormozi on branding: deliberate pairings that raise prices, conversion and loyalty
summary: Hormozi defines branding in actionable terms: a deliberate pairing of your product with outcomes your ideal customer likes. Good branding drives premium pricing, better ad response and loyalty. He explains how to build it by curating pairings, recovering from bad ones, and measuring influence, direction and reach.

principles.text: Branding is a deliberate pairing of your business with outcomes your ideal customer wants; good branding means pairing with good outcomes.
principles.quote: branding is a deliberate pairing of things through an outcome

principles.text: Advertising is letting people know; branding is the pairing that results. You can have good advertising and bad branding.
principles.quote: advertising is letting people know about your stuff branding is the pairing that occurs as a result so it was good advertising but bad branding

principles.text: A strong brand gives pricing power, better ad response, and loyalty that protects against competitors.
principles.quote: good branding drives that premium pricing good branding also improves advertising

principles.text: Pair deliberately and stay focused; random, distant pairings weaken a brand. Add the good and pull out the bad.
principles.quote: distant and random pairings hurt a brand because they're so hard to make the associations with

principles.text: Recover from a bad pairing by overwhelming it with more of what your audience likes, not by trying to erase it.
principles.quote: what we try to do is just overwhelm it with way more of the stuff that the majority of our people actually like

principles.text: Premium brands must deliver on the product; brand carries a good-enough product, but a weak one loses repeat purchases.
principles.quote: it's not going to keep the business you'll get the first purchase you just won't get the ones after that
